author: opencode-worker-3
text: DECISION ANALYSIS (worker-3, verified both implementations this round): The divergence is real and exact — C lichen_rpl_dodag_process_dio (dodag.c:406-412) ignores a foreign DODAG's DIO regardless of join state (test main.c:455 + :501 pin rejection), while Python DodagState.process_dio (dodag.py:413-426) ADOPTS the foreign DODAGID on unjoined first contact (test dodag.py:431-444 pins adoption). The C comment (dodag.c:400-405) states 'An UNJOINED node may first-join a foreign DODAG' — contradicting its own code. OPTIONS: (A) Canonical = ADOPT (RFC 6550 8.2.1/3.2.3 + LICHEN's TOFU trust model + the C code's own documented intent): an unjoined node joins any DODAG whose DIO passes link authentication; C dodag.c foreign-handling changes for the unjoined case only + C tests :455/:501 flip + comment fixed; Python unchanged. Risk: a provisioned leaf hearing a rogue-but-signed DODAG switches allegiance — mitigated by the signature requirement (DIO must be from an authenticated peer). (B) Canonical = REJECT-foreign-until-pinned: C stays, Python's adoption path changes + its test flips; matches out-of-band provisioning deployments but breaks mesh self-formation without provisioning and deviates from RFC join semantics. RECOMMENDATION: (A) — consistent with RFC 6550, LICHEN's no-provisioning TOFU design, and the C comment's stated intent; requires a normative sentence in spec/05 8.2 (DODAG topology: unjoined nodes adopt any authenticated DIO's DODAGID). Decision is Mark's (join-semantics + RFC deviation weight).
